Theorem
[Lichnerowicz identity for the curvature tensor]

Source: petersen:page-0362, petersen:page-0363 ↗ def:pet-ch9-lichnerowicz-laplacian ↗ def:pet-ch9-weitzenbock-curvature-operator 1. ch9:9.4.2For the curvature tensor, the Lichnerowicz operator with coefficient $ frac 12$ satisfies egin{align*} ( abla ^* abla R)(X,Y,Z,W)+ frac 12\operatorname {Ric}(R)(X,Y,Z,W) & = frac 12( abla _X abla ^*R)(Y,Z,W)- frac 12( abla _Y abla ^*R)(X,Z,W)\ & \quad + frac 12( abla _Z abla ^*R)(W,X,Y)- frac 12( abla _W abla ^*R)(Z,X,Y). \end{align*} Thus the $c= frac 12$ Lichnerowicz Laplacian of $R$ vanishes whenever $ abla ^*R=0$; curvature is Lichnerowicz-harmonic exactly in this divergence-free case.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch9-curvature-tensor-lichnerowicz \sketch Evaluate in a normal frame and apply the second Bianchi identity to the two differentiated curvature slots. Commuting the resulting second covariant derivatives contributes the Weitzenböck term. Repeating the computation after interchanging the pair $(X,Y)$ with $(Z,W)$, and averaging by the pair symmetry of $R$, gives exactly the four divergence derivatives on the right and the coefficient $ frac 12\operatorname {Ric}(R)$. If $ abla ^*R=0$, all four terms vanish.

□
